label: Ranking of candidate layouts under the stand-in simulator (not a global optimum)

objective.definition: objective_m = P90 positioning error (m) + anchor_cost_m x anchors. Ranked low to high; ties by median, then fewer anchors.
objective.note: Default cost 0: layouts are ranked by P90 error alone, so the Pareto front shows what extra anchors buy.

crowd_model_description: Usable range along a path = assumed range x max(0.5, 1 - 0.1 x mean density on the path), where density is in people per m2.
Usable anchors needed at a cell = base requirement + min(2, ceil(density at the cell / 2)), and no extra where density is 0.
Where crowd zones overlap, the higher density applies.
These coefficients are planning assumptions chosen by the planner author. They are not measured and not yet aligned with the simulator's crowd formula.
assumptions: A walkable grid cell counts as covered when at least 3 anchors are within 15 m of its centre with no traced wall or obstacle in between.
Grid resolution is 1 m; each cell is judged at its centre only, so small gaps inside a cell can be missed.
Range is an assumed hard limit set by the user, not a measured value. Real range varies with noise, obstructions and crowds.
Every traced wall blocks completely. Walls that were not traced do not exist in this model.
Anchors may only be placed at the 350 candidate positions tested (on a regular floor lattice, spacing 2 m, at least 0.2 m from any wall).
A 'proven' minimum holds only for that candidate set, grid and range; other positions could need fewer anchors.
Positioning error is simulated with a stand-in simulator and the mock predictor. It is not a measurement and not a Traceline result.
Anchor positions are chosen from a finite candidate set, so the ranking is the best of the layouts tested.

evaluation_set.note: Walks are seeded random walks through the walkable area. Development set only: never the hidden set.

slot_policy.text: Up to 8 anchor slots per step. With more anchors than slots, the 8 anchors with the smallest measured valid range are used (ties by anchor id), and unused slots are padded with anchors that have no reading. Measured ranges only; truth is never used.

warnings: Simulated geometric coverage only. It is not a guarantee of radio performance: walls, crowds, equipment and interference change real signals. Run a site survey before installing anything.
No layout that meets the criterion fits the 8 model slots. The smallest one found needs 19 anchors.
The best layout (L06) needs 21 anchors. The model takes at most 8 slots, so the simulation uses the slot policy above and the venue file cannot be exported with it (DECISIONS 39).
Layouts above 8 anchors are simulated with the slot policy; that is an assumption until the team decides how a larger layout feeds an 8-slot model.
Positioning errors come from a stand-in simulator and the mock predictor. They are not Traceline results and not measurements.
Some crowd zones had no density and use the fallback density you entered.
Only 90 simulated steps fall inside crowd zones, so the inside-crowd error is indicative only. Use longer walks or more trajectories.
notes: Layouts are compared on the same walks, with the same noise on shared anchors (common random numbers), so a difference comes from geometry and layout.
Crowd effects are placeholders in the stand-in simulator. They change simulated error inside crowd zones, so that comparison depends on them.
Naive grid: evenly spaced, snapped to the same candidate positions. Not counted in any search budget.
